metaTitle: Toni's Sushi Bar Instagram Case Study | Button Up Media
metaDescription: How Button Up Media grew Toni's Sushi Bar on Instagram from about 4K to 80K followers in five months, with chef-led Reels that drew 64M+ views on South Beach.
ldHeadline: Toni's Sushi Bar: from about 4K to 80K Instagram followers in five months
h1Sub: 4K to 80K Instagram followers in five months
answer: We made Toni's Sushi Bar's chef a teacher on Instagram. In five months, followers grew from about 4K to 80K and our 22 Reels drew 64M+ views.

metrics.label: Instagram followers, up from about 4K
metrics.meaning: About 4,000 people followed @tonissushi when our first Reel went up on June 18, 2026. Five months later, on Nov 16, 2026, it was 80,100: about 20 times as many.

metrics.label: Reel views in five months
metrics.meaning: We added up the views Instagram shows on all 22 Reels we posted from June 18 to Nov 16, 2026. They also collected 1.9M+ likes.

metrics.meaning: The chef's sushi etiquette lesson, posted Aug 19, 2026. 1.6M people liked it, and it now sits pinned at the top of the profile.

paragraphs: Toni's has been family-run on South Beach since 1987, when Hiromi “Toni” Takarada opened it, according to Miami New Times. Its Instagram calls it South Beach's original sushi bar.

That history wasn't showing up where visitors now pick a place to eat: their phones. The account had about 4,000 followers, and its last posts before we started, in February 2026, got 12 to 156 likes each.

items.title: Make the chef the teacher
items.bodyHtml: Chef Toshiya is a sushi chef from Japan, and on camera he teaches the Japanese way to eat sushi: soy sauce on the fish, not the rice; ginger between pieces, not with every bite; why rubbing your chopsticks together isn't needed.

items.title: Teach one thing per Reel
items.bodyHtml: Each video answers a question people didn't know they had: real wasabi versus the green paste, sashimi versus temaki versus nigiri, the three cuts of bluefin tuna. A short lesson is easy to save and send to a friend, so it travels far past the people who already follow.

items.title: Let the lessons do the selling
items.bodyHtml: No Reel says “come eat here.” Watching a chef from Japan show the proper way to eat sushi tells viewers, without a word of selling, that Toni's is the real deal and worth a visit.

items.title: Turn views into visits
items.bodyHtml: Every Reel carries the address, 1208 Washington Ave, in the comments. On the etiquette Reel that comment alone has 2,624 likes. Stories are built to convert, pointing people who just watched toward the restaurant and how to get there.
